findings.title: Template variables and ad hoc filters are now applied twice per query
findings.body:
`runSplitQuery` now runs `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target. The sub-requests then go to `datasource.runQuery`, whose backend query path runs `applyTemplateVariables` on each target again.

Interpolation is therefore not a single pass:
- The ad hoc filters in `request.filters` are injected twice, for example `{a="b", k="v", k="v"}` or a duplicated `| k="v"` stage.
- Variable values that contain `$...` text are re-interpolated after the first pass.

The result is altered or bloated LogQL that differs from what the user configured. Either interpolate once and skip it downstream, or interpolate a copy only for classification (log vs. metric, step, selector) and send the original targets.

findings.title: Shard splitting interpolates again before delegating to runSplitQuery, which interpolates again
findings.body:
`runShardSplitQuery` calls `applyTemplateVariables` with `request.filters` and passes the result to `splitQueriesByStreamShard`. That function calls `runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest)`, which now calls `applyTemplateVariables` again with the same `subRequest.filters`. Finally `datasource.runQuery` applies it a third time.

The previous code used `interpolateVariablesInQueries` without filters, so ad hoc filters were added only once. Now the same filters can be injected two or three times into each sharded query, and variable output gets re-interpolated.

The updated test even locks this in by expecting `applyTemplateVariables` to be called 5 times for a single target (line 112). Its mock is idempotent, so the repeated application is hidden.
